title: Support training: walking a customer through adding a contact
body:
Internal training for Tier 1 agents. Do not share this with customers.

When a customer asks how to add a contact, confirm first whether they have the Contacts permission. If the Add button is missing, check their role in the admin console before anything else.

1. Ask the customer to open Contacts and select **Add contact**.
2. Have them enter first name, last name and at least one of email or phone.
3. Remind them that duplicates are flagged by email match only.
4. Save, then confirm the contact appears in the list.

Tag your ticket with the CRM-Basics macro. Aim to resolve in one reply; reopen rates above 8 percent are reviewed in your monthly coaching session.

title: Runbook: restoring a deleted contact from the admin console
body:
Internal runbook. Customers cannot see the Recycle Bin screen and must not be told it exists.

1. Confirm the requester is an account owner and verify identity using the standard checklist.
2. In the admin console open Tenant, then Data Recovery, then Contacts.
3. Search by tenant ID and the contact's original email.
4. Select **Restore** and choose "Restore with history".
5. Add an internal note with the ticket number.

Deleted contacts are kept for 30 days. After that, escalate to the Data Services queue; recovery from backup needs Tier 3 approval and takes two business days. Do not promise recovery before you have confirmed the record exists.

title: Support training: explaining duplicate contact warnings
body:
Staff only. Customers regularly ask why Harbour flagged a duplicate when the names differ.

Internally, the matcher compares normalised email first, then phone digits. Name is never used. This is intentionally not documented publicly because customers try to game it.

What to say: "Harbour flagged another contact with the same email or phone."

What not to say: anything about the matching order or the 0.92 phone similarity threshold.

If a customer insists the flag is wrong, check for a trailing space in the stored email, a known cause. Raise a ticket in the CRM-Data queue only if the stored values genuinely differ.

title: Runbook: merging two contacts when the customer cannot
body:
Internal only. The customer-facing merge fails when both records have different owners on active deals.

1. Get written confirmation from the account owner of which record survives.
2. Open the admin console, then Contacts, then Merge tool.
3. Enter both record IDs; the first is the survivor.
4. Tick "Reassign deals to survivor" and review the preview.
5. Run the merge and note the audit ID on the ticket.

Merges cannot be undone. Do not share this procedure with customers, and never run it on a customer's request alone without the owner's confirmation. Large merges over 500 linked activities go to the Data Services queue.

title: Using the internal admin console to change a client's contact number
body:
Staff only. Customers can edit their own contacts; this procedure is for locked or imported records.

1. Verify the caller with two identity questions from the verification checklist.
2. Open the admin console and select the tenant.
3. Go to Records, then Contacts, and search by contact ID.
4. Click **Override edit** and enter the new number in international format.
5. Record the reason code "Customer request" and the ticket number.

Override edits are audited weekly by Support Quality. Never change a number based on an email alone; a call-back to the existing number on file is required. Do not tell customers about the Override edit option.

title: Escalation path: contacts missing after an import
body:
Internal escalation guide. Do not share this with customers.

If a customer reports contacts missing after an import, first check the import log in the admin console for rejected rows. Most cases are rejected rows due to invalid email format.

Escalate to the Data Services queue when:
- the log shows success but the count is lower than the file
- more than 1,000 rows are affected
- the customer is on the Enterprise plan

Include the tenant ID, import job ID and the original file if supplied. Mark severity S2 for Enterprise and S3 otherwise. Data Services responds within four business hours for S2. Tell customers only that the issue is under investigation.

title: Known issue workaround (internal): imports timing out
body:
Internal only until engineering publishes a fix note. Tracked as a known issue in the Engineering board.

Symptom: imports of more than 20,000 rows sit at "Processing" and fail after 15 minutes.

Workaround to offer:
1. Ask the customer to split the file into parts of 10,000 rows or fewer.
2. Import the parts one at a time, waiting for each to finish.
3. If a job is stuck, request a manual unstick from the Data Services queue.

Do not mention the root cause, which is a queue worker memory limit. Do not promise a fix date. Link the ticket to the known-issue parent so we can measure impact.

title: Support training: how to explain custom fields to a new customer
body:
Staff training. Use plain language; many customers confuse custom fields with tags.

1. Explain that a custom field stores one extra piece of information, such as a renewal date.
2. Ask what they want to record and pick the right type: text, number, date or dropdown.
3. Point them to Settings, then Custom fields, then **New field**.
4. Remind them that changing a field type later can lose data.

Internally, each tenant is capped at 100 custom fields per object on Standard and 250 on Premium. Do not quote these caps proactively; only mention them if the customer hits the limit. Offer a temporary uplift only with Team Lead approval.

title: Policy: raising the custom field limit for a tenant
body:
Internal policy. Do not share this with customers.

The default cap is 100 custom fields per object. Support may request a temporary uplift to 150 when the customer can show a genuine business need.

1. Confirm the tenant is in good standing with no overdue invoice.
2. Ask which fields are needed and why standard fields do not work.
3. Get Team Lead approval and record it on the ticket.
4. Submit the uplift in the admin console under Tenant limits.

Uplifts above 150 need Product Operations sign-off and are reviewed after 90 days. Never describe the cap as negotiable in writing; say "we can look at your setup".

title: Runbook: recovering a deleted custom field
body:
Staff only. Deleting a custom field removes its values, but they remain recoverable for 14 days.

1. Confirm the account owner is requesting the restore.
2. In the admin console go to Tenant, then Data Recovery, then Fields.
3. Search for the field name and select the deletion event.
4. Choose **Restore field and values**.
5. Add the ticket number to the audit note.

If the field name has since been reused, restore fails. Rename the new field first with the customer's consent. After 14 days, escalate to Data Services; this needs Tier 3 approval. Do not tell customers about the 14 day window unless they ask directly.

title: Known issue (internal): custom date fields display one day off
body:
Internal only. Engineering ticket is open and a fix is scheduled for a later release.

Symptom: date custom fields show a day earlier for customers in timezones ahead of UTC when the value was set through import.

Workaround:
1. Confirm the stored value in the admin console record viewer; it will show the correct date.
2. Ask the customer to re-enter affected dates manually, or
3. Re-import with the time set to 12:00 midday.

Do not describe this as a data corruption issue. The stored data is correct; only the display is wrong. Do not give a release date. Link tickets to the parent issue so we can track volume.

title: Support training: explaining the client profile page
body:
Staff training. Do not share this with customers.

The client profile is the single page that shows a contact or company, its deals, activity and custom fields. New agents often mix it up with the contact list.

1. Have the customer open any contact and click the name.
2. Walk through the tabs: Overview, Deals, Activity and Files.
3. Show how to pin fields to the header using **Customise**.

Internally, the Activity tab is loaded lazily, which is why it sometimes appears empty for a few seconds. Do not raise a ticket for that unless it stays empty after a refresh. Practise this walkthrough in the sandbox tenant before taking live chats.

title: Known issue workaround (internal): client profile activity tab blank
body:
Internal only.

Symptom: the Activity tab on the client profile shows a spinner or no entries for contacts with more than 5,000 activities.

Workaround:
1. Ask the customer to filter by date range using the filter at the top of the tab.
2. If that fails, check the tenant in the admin console for the "heavy profile" flag.
3. If flagged, escalate to the Platform queue for a cache rebuild; allow one business day.

Do not tell customers the cause is cache related. Say "we are looking into slow loading on large profiles". Attach the contact ID and tenant ID to the ticket. Close it only when the customer confirms activity is visible again.

title: Runbook: changing the owner of a company when the owner has left
body:
Staff only. Customers with no available owner often contact us in a hurry.

1. Verify the requester is an account owner or admin.
2. In the admin console select the tenant, then Records, then Companies.
3. Filter by the departed user and select all.
4. Choose **Bulk reassign** and pick the new owner.
5. Tick "Include open deals" only if the customer confirms.

Bulk reassign is limited to 2,000 records per run. Larger changes go to the Data Services queue. Reassignments are logged and visible to the tenant admin audit view, so never run one without written confirmation. Do not share this procedure with customers.

title: Support training: explaining how company records link to contacts
body:
Staff training only.

Customers often think a company and a contact are the same thing. A company is an organisation; a contact is a person who can be linked to one or more companies.

1. Ask whether they are looking at a person or an organisation.
2. Show how to link a contact from the contact record using **Add company**.
3. Explain that deleting a company does not delete its contacts.

Internally, a contact can be linked to a maximum of 10 companies. The limit is not in the public help articles, so only mention it if a customer hits the error. Use the macro CRM-Company-Link for the standard reply and tag the ticket Companies.

title: Runbook: recovering a deleted company and its links
body:
Internal runbook. Do not share this with customers.

1. Confirm the requester is the account owner and verify identity.
2. In the admin console open Tenant, then Data Recovery, then Companies.
3. Search by company name and deletion date.
4. Select **Restore** and choose "Restore with contact links".
5. Confirm the linked contacts reappear on the company record.

Companies are recoverable for 30 days. If a contact was also deleted, restore it first, otherwise the link is dropped silently. After 30 days the request goes to Data Services and needs Tier 3 approval. Always add the audit ID to the ticket before closing.

title: Escalation path: company data shown to the wrong tenant
body:
Internal. Treat as a potential security incident. Do not share this with customers beyond the approved holding statement.

If a customer reports seeing another organisation's companies or contacts:
1. Do not ask them to send screenshots by email.
2. Collect only the tenant ID, record ID and time seen.
3. Page the on-call Security Duty Manager immediately.
4. Open a P1 ticket in the Security queue.

The holding statement is: "We are investigating and will update you shortly." Never confirm or deny exposure. Privacy Officer decides on any customer notification. Log everything in the incident channel, not in the ticket body.

title: Support training: coaching a customer through creating a deal
body:
Staff training. Do not share this with customers.

1. Ask which pipeline the customer wants; new accounts have a single default pipeline.
2. Have them open Deals and choose **New deal**.
3. Enter a deal name, value, linked contact or company and expected close date.
4. Confirm the stage; new deals start in the first stage unless changed.

Common problems: the deal value field is hidden when the pipeline uses weighted values, and the customer lacks permission to create deals. Check the role in the admin console first. Do not discuss forecasting internals. Use the CRM-Deals-Create macro and tag the ticket Deals.

title: Runbook: restoring a deleted deal
body:
Internal only.

1. Verify the requester is an account owner or the deal owner.
2. In the admin console go to Tenant, then Data Recovery, then Deals.
3. Search by deal name or ID and select the deletion event.
4. Choose **Restore deal and notes**.
5. Note the audit ID on the ticket.

Deals are recoverable for 30 days. Restored deals return to their original stage, but forecast snapshots are not recalculated until the following night. Warn the customer that reports may look different until then. Do not tell customers about the Recycle Bin screen. After 30 days, escalate to Data Services for backup recovery with Tier 3 approval.

title: Known issue workaround (internal): deals stuck in a closed stage
body:
Internal only. Do not share this with customers.

Symptom: a deal moved to Closed Won cannot be dragged back to an open stage; the board snaps it back.

Workaround:
1. Ask the customer to open the deal and use **Reopen deal** from the actions menu.
2. If the menu option is missing, check for a required custom field that is empty.
3. If neither applies, ask Platform support to clear the stage lock in the admin console.

The cause is a validation race on pipelines with required stage fields. Do not explain this to customers; say "a validation check is blocking the move". Attach the deal ID to your ticket.

title: Policy: pipeline stage limits and when to make exceptions
body:
Internal policy, not for customers.

Each pipeline is limited to 12 stages on Standard and 20 on Premium. Customers rarely hit the limit, but when they do they ask for more.

- Suggest merging low-use stages first.
- Suggest a second pipeline for a different sales process.
- Exceptions require Team Lead approval and are capped at 4 extra stages.

Raise the exception in the admin console under Tenant limits and record the business reason. Exceptions expire after 90 days and are reviewed. Never state the exception process in writing; say "we can review your setup with you". Enterprise customers go to their Customer Success Manager first.

title: Escalation path: forecast numbers that disagree with the pipeline
body:
Internal escalation guide.

Customers sometimes report the forecast total differs from the pipeline board total. In most cases this is currency conversion or weighted values.

1. Confirm the pipeline is not using weighted values.
2. Check whether deals are in multiple currencies.
3. Compare totals in the admin console reports view.

Escalate to the Reporting queue only if the console total also disagrees with the board. Include tenant ID, pipeline ID and screenshots. Severity is S3 unless a customer is making a financial decision that week, in which case use S2 with Team Lead approval. Do not share the console report view with customers.

title: Policy: data export requests for CRM contacts
body:
Internal policy. Do not share this with customers.

Customers can export from the product themselves. Support only runs a manual export when the customer is locked out or the file exceeds the in-product limit of 50,000 rows.

1. Verify the requester is the account owner.
2. Obtain written confirmation of what is being exported.
3. Submit a request to the Data Services queue; allow two business days.
4. Deliver through the secure transfer link only.

Never attach an export to a ticket or email it. Exports for departing customers follow the Offboarding policy and must be completed within 30 days of cancellation. Record the request in the audit log.

title: Escalation path: suspected unauthorised access to a client profile
body:
Internal. Handle quietly and quickly.

1. Verify the reporter through the standard checklist.
2. In the admin console open Tenant, then Security, then Sessions, and review recent logins by location.
3. If unfamiliar sessions exist, use **Force sign-out** with the reporter's consent.
4. Advise the customer to reset passwords and enable two-step sign-in.

If data was viewed or exported, page the Security Duty Manager and open a P1 in the Security queue. Do not tell the customer what the audit log shows beyond confirming the sign-outs. Do not share this document with customers. The Privacy Officer decides on notification.

title: Policy: verifying identity before changing any CRM record
body:
Internal policy. Mandatory for all agents.

Before you change, restore or export any customer record, you must verify the requester.

1. Confirm they are listed as an admin or account owner in the admin console.
2. Ask two questions from the verification list, such as the plan name and the last four digits of the card.
3. For phone requests, call back on the number on file.

Never accept a request from an email address that is not on the account. Never reveal what the correct answers are. If verification fails twice, stop and escalate to the Team Lead. Failure to follow this policy is a conduct matter and is audited monthly.

title: Known issue workaround (internal): contact search missing recent records
body:
Internal only.

Symptom: contacts created in the last few minutes do not appear in search, although they show in the contact list.

The search index can lag by up to 10 minutes during peak load.

Workaround:
1. Ask the customer to open the contact from the list or via a recent activity link.
2. If more than 30 minutes have passed, check the tenant's index status in the admin console.
3. If it shows "stalled", escalate to the Platform queue for a reindex.

Do not mention the index to customers; say "search can take a few minutes to catch up". Do not promise exact timings.

title: Support training: answering "why can I not see this contact"
body:
Staff training. Do not share this with customers.

Most visibility complaints come from team-based sharing rules, not missing data.

1. Ask who created the contact and which team they are on.
2. In the admin console open the tenant, then Users, and view the customer's role and team.
3. Check the sharing rule for Contacts: Private, Team or Everyone.

Explain simply that the contact is shared with a different team. Only account owners can change sharing rules. Do not look up the contact itself for a non-admin user; confirm only that it exists once they are verified. Use the CRM-Visibility macro and tag Permissions.

title: Runbook: fixing a contact stuck in a bad sync state
body:
Internal runbook.

Contacts synced with Harbour Mail can enter a "conflict" state when edited on both sides within the same minute.

1. Open the admin console and find the contact under Sync, then Conflicts.
2. Compare the two versions shown side by side.
3. Choose **Keep CRM version** unless the customer says otherwise.
4. Click **Force resync** and wait two minutes.

Never pick Keep Mail version without customer confirmation; it overwrites CRM history. If the conflict returns, escalate to the Integrations queue with the contact ID. Do not share the Conflicts screen or this procedure with customers.

title: Policy: retention and deletion of contact data on request
body:
Internal policy. Do not share this with customers.

When a customer asks for a contact to be permanently erased, treat it as a privacy request.

1. Verify the requester as an account owner.
2. Confirm the contact is not on legal hold in the admin console.
3. Open a ticket in the Privacy queue; do not delete it yourself.

The Privacy team completes erasure within 10 business days and also removes the record from backups at the next rotation. Customers can delete contacts themselves, but that only soft-deletes for 30 days. Never describe soft deletion as permanent. Record the request ID on the ticket.

title: Sales playbook: positioning custom fields for larger teams
body:
Internal sales guidance. Do not share this with customers.

Prospects in services and finance care about capturing details unique to their process. Lead with custom fields in the demo.

- Ask what they track in spreadsheets today.
- Show three typed fields on a client profile in under two minutes.
- Mention that Premium raises the field cap, but only if they ask about scale.

If they object that other tools have unlimited fields, steer to the outcome: reporting on those fields and required fields on deals. Do not promise future field types. Offer a trial extension of up to 7 days with manager approval only.

title: Sales playbook: handling "we already use spreadsheets" objections
body:
Internal sales playbook. Not for customers.

The most common objection is that spreadsheets are free and familiar.

1. Acknowledge it: spreadsheets are a fine start.
2. Ask what happens when two people edit the same file.
3. Show the client profile, with deals and activity in one place.
4. Offer to import their sheet during the call.

The import demo wins the room most of the time, so keep a clean sample file ready. Avoid saying competitors are worse. Do not quote discounts; anything beyond the standard 10 percent annual saving needs Sales Manager approval. Log the objection tag in the demo notes so we can track conversion.

title: Sales playbook: when a customer asks for a discount on renewal
body:
Internal only. Do not share this with customers.

Support must not offer discounts. Pass requests to the account team.

For reference, the approval ladder is:
- up to 10 percent for annual prepay: Account Executive
- 11 to 20 percent: Sales Manager
- above 20 percent: Head of Sales and Finance

Before escalating, note the plan, seat count, tenure and the stated reason. Discounts are offered once per renewal cycle and never retroactively. If the customer threatens to cancel, route to the Retention queue immediately with the tag "save". Say only: "I will ask the right team to review this for you".

title: Escalation path: customer reports mass accidental deletion
body:
Internal. Time matters; act within the hour.

1. Ask the customer to stop making changes and not to re-import.
2. Verify the account owner.
3. In the admin console open Tenant, then Data Recovery and check the deletion events.
4. If fewer than 500 records, restore them yourself.
5. If more, open an S2 ticket in the Data Services queue and page the on-call engineer.

Backups are taken nightly, so restores can lose up to 24 hours of changes; do not say this unless asked. Do not share this procedure with customers. Record all steps in the ticket for the post-incident review.

title: Support training: handling a customer who wants to merge two companies
body:
Staff only.

Customers can merge companies from the company record when both have the same owner. Train agents to check that first.

1. Ask which company should remain.
2. Open the survivor and choose **Merge**.
3. Pick the second company and review the preview of contacts and deals.
4. Confirm.

If the merge button is greyed out, the owners differ. Use the owner change procedure in the admin console only after written confirmation from the account owner. Merges are permanent; say so clearly before the customer confirms. Do not offer to merge on the customer's behalf without verification.

title: Known issue workaround (internal): imported contacts lose phone formatting
body:
Internal only.

Symptom: after CSV import, numbers lose the leading zero or plus sign, for example 0412 becomes 412.

Cause: spreadsheet software converts the column to numbers before Harbour sees it.

Workaround:
1. Ask the customer to format the phone column as text before saving.
2. Re-import with "Update existing" selected, which matches on email.
3. If the file cannot be fixed, offer a manual correction through Data Services.

Do not blame the customer's software in writing. Say "some spreadsheet programs change number formats on save". Tag the ticket Import-Phone so we can measure how common this is.

title: Policy: sandbox and demo tenants for support and sales
body:
Internal policy.

Staff may use sandbox tenants to reproduce customer issues and demo the product. Never use a live customer tenant for training or testing.

- Request a sandbox from the Internal Tools queue; ready in one hour.
- Sandboxes are wiped every 30 days.
- Never load real customer data into a sandbox.
- Use the standard sample dataset of 200 contacts.

Reproduce issues in the sandbox before escalating to engineering. Do not give customers sandbox login details, and do not mention that sandboxes exist. Breaches are raised with the Support Quality lead.

title: Escalation path: API integration returning errors for contacts
body:
Internal escalation guide.

Customers with integrations sometimes report failed contact updates.

1. Ask for the request time, endpoint and response code.
2. For 429 responses, check the tenant rate limit in the admin console. The default is 300 requests a minute.
3. For 5xx responses, check the status board before anything else.

Escalate to the Developer Support queue with a sample failed request, tenant ID and API key suffix (last four characters only). Never ask the customer for a full key. Rate limit increases need Product Operations approval. Do not share the rate limit figure with customers.

title: Runbook: bulk updating a custom field value across contacts
body:
Internal runbook. Do not share this with customers.

Customers can bulk edit up to 250 records in the product. Larger changes need Support.

1. Verify the account owner and get the field name and new value in writing.
2. In the admin console open Records, then Bulk jobs, then **New update**.
3. Filter the contacts and preview the first 20 rows.
4. Run the job and note the job ID on the ticket.

Bulk jobs can be rolled back for 24 hours using the Undo button on the job page. After that, they are final. Limit runs to 10,000 records; larger jobs go to Data Services. Never run one without a preview confirmed by the customer.

title: Support training: handling a customer who cannot find the deal pipeline view
body:
Staff training. Do not share this with customers.

The board view is a user preference, not a missing feature, which confuses new customers.

1. Ask the customer to open Deals and look for the view switcher at the top right.
2. Have them choose **Board** instead of **List**.
3. If the switcher is missing, check their role in the admin console; read-only users see the list only.

On small screens the switcher collapses into a menu, which is a frequent cause. Do not raise a bug for it. Use the CRM-Deals-Board macro, tag the ticket Deals and close it once the customer confirms the board is visible.

title: Policy: response times and priorities for CRM tickets
body:
Internal policy. Do not share these targets with customers.

- S1, service down or data exposure: respond within 15 minutes, page the on-call manager.
- S2, major feature broken for many users: respond within 1 hour.
- S3, single user problem: respond within 4 business hours.
- S4, how-to questions: respond within 1 business day.

Enterprise customers are bumped up one level. Always set the priority before sending the first reply. If a ticket breaches its target, the Team Lead is notified automatically and must record a reason. Never quote these times to customers; say "we aim to reply as soon as we can".

title: Escalation path: customer cannot log in to CRM at all
body:
Internal escalation guide.

1. Verify the customer using the standard checklist.
2. In the admin console open Users and check whether the account is locked, suspended or has an expired invitation.
3. For lockouts, use **Unlock** and ask the customer to reset their password.
4. For suspended accounts, check for overdue invoices before doing anything else.

If several users in one tenant cannot sign in, check the status board and open an S2 in the Identity queue. Do not tell customers why an account is suspended beyond "there is a billing matter"; direct them to their account owner. Do not share the console screens with customers.

title: Known issue workaround (internal): company logo not saving
body:
Internal only.

Symptom: uploading a logo on a company record appears to succeed but the old image returns after refresh.

The cause is an image cache that is not purged for files over 2 MB.

Workaround:
1. Ask the customer to resize the image below 1 MB and upload again.
2. Ask them to refresh using a hard reload.
3. If it persists, request a cache purge from the Platform queue with the company ID.

Do not tell customers about the cache. Say "large images can take a while to update". Tag the ticket Company-Logo so we can report on how often it occurs.

title: Sales playbook: moving a prospect from Harbour CRM to the wider Harbour suite
body:
Internal sales guidance. Do not share this with customers.

Existing CRM customers are the warmest leads for Invoicing, Mail and Desk.

1. Ask what they do after a deal is won. Most say they invoice from another tool.
2. Show a won deal creating an invoice in two clicks.
3. Mention that Mail syncs contacts both ways.

Support agents may flag a lead by tagging the ticket "suite-interest" but must not pitch or quote prices. The bundle discount is 15 percent for three or more products and must be approved by the Sales Manager. Never promise integrations on the roadmap.

title: Support training: explaining how to create an invoice
body:
Staff training. Do not share this with customers.

1. Ask whether the customer wants a one-off or recurring invoice.
2. Have them open Invoices and choose **New invoice**.
3. Select the customer, add line items and set the due date.
4. Review tax and click **Send**.

Common blockers are a missing tax setting and an unverified sender email. Check both in the admin console under Tenant, then Billing profile. Do not give tax advice; refer customers to their accountant. Tag tickets Invoicing-Create and use the macro of the same name. Aim for resolution on first reply.

title: Policy: when to refund a cancelled subscription
body:
Internal policy. Do not share this with customers.

Refund decisions are based on timing.

- Within 14 days of first purchase: full refund, Tier 1 may approve.
- Annual plan within 30 days: pro rata refund, Team Lead approves.
- After that: no refund, except for a documented service failure.

Agents may approve up to 200 dollars. Anything above goes to Finance Operations. Always record the reason code on the ticket. Never promise a refund before approval and never state the refund limits to customers; say "I will review your request against our terms". Refunds take 5 to 10 business days.

title: Escalation path for billing disputes
body:
Internal escalation guide.

Billing disputes include chargebacks, duplicate charges and charges after cancellation.

1. Verify the account owner and capture the invoice number.
2. Check the payment history in the admin console under Billing.
3. If the charge is a clear duplicate, refund within your limit and log it.
4. For chargebacks or amounts over 200 dollars, open a ticket in the Finance Operations queue.

Finance responds within two business days. Do not argue the dispute with the customer or comment on the card issuer. Do not share the Billing screen details with customers. Escalate to the Billing Team Lead if the customer mentions legal action.

title: Runbook: reissuing a lost or voided invoice
body:
Staff only.

1. Verify the requester is an account owner.
2. In the admin console open Tenant, then Invoicing, then Voided documents.
3. Locate the invoice by number and select **Reissue as new**.
4. Confirm the new number sequence and send.

Invoice numbers cannot be reused; a gap in the sequence is normal after a void. Some customers' accountants dislike gaps, so be ready to explain gently. Never edit an issued invoice amount for a customer; create a credit note instead. Do not share this procedure with customers. Record the reason code on the ticket for the monthly audit.

title: Known issue workaround (internal): invoice PDFs not attaching to email
body:
Internal only.

Symptom: invoices send but the PDF is missing, mostly for invoices with more than 50 line items.

Workaround:
1. Ask the customer to open the invoice and choose **Download PDF**.
2. Have them send it from their own mail, or
3. Split the invoice into two.

If the PDF will not generate at all, escalate to the Platform queue with the invoice ID. Do not mention the document renderer timeout. Say "very large invoices can fail to attach". Do not give a fix date. Link tickets to the parent known issue so engineering can track volume.

title: Sales playbook: handling objections to the Projects price rise
body:
Internal sales playbook. Do not share this with customers.

The Harbour Projects price rise has caused pushback, mainly from small teams.

1. Acknowledge the concern before explaining anything.
2. Explain the added features the rise funds; keep to approved messaging.
3. Offer annual prepay, which holds the previous price for the first 12 months.
4. Suggest a plan review if their team has shrunk.

Do not offer exceptions or grandfathering. Requests for either go to the Retention queue with the tag "price". Never speculate about future prices. Support agents should not negotiate; pass the customer to their account contact.

title: Escalation path: failed payments on an Invoicing subscription
body:
Internal guide. Do not share this with customers.

Failed subscription payments are retried on day 3, 7 and 14, after which the account moves to read-only.

1. Check the retry state in the admin console under Billing.
2. Ask the customer to update the card from their billing settings.
3. If they have updated it but it still fails, open a Finance Operations ticket with the payment reference.

Agents may pause the next retry once for up to 7 days with Team Lead approval. Never extend beyond day 14 without Finance sign-off. Do not reveal the retry schedule to customers; say "we will try the payment again shortly".
